Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Pilot pricing proposal and onboarding plan

Hi Jane,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, attached is a short pilot MA and a recommended pricing structure for HelioHealth's 12-week POC. Key points:

- Pilot duration: 12 weeks, up to 10M tokens/month (avg seq 512)
- Standard list price: $0.010/token. To accelerate the pilot we're proposing a blended pilot rate of $0.0035/token (65% off list) for the first 12 weeks.
- Onboarding credit: $15k support/onboarding credit applied as one-time invoice offset.
- Success metrics: latency SLO 200ms p90, integration milestones in attached plan.

This discount is outside our standard guardrails, so I'll need a quick internal signoff. Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether you need a PO? Also, procurement asked whether we can cap the per-token rate if usage spikes; we've included a rate ceiling in option A.

I've attached: HelioHealth_Pilot_MA_plan.xlsx and a clean pricing options CSV. Happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through.

Best,
Diego
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- HelioHealth_Pilot_MA_plan.xlsx (xlsx)
- Pricing_Options_A_B.csv (csv)

From: Jane Porter <jane.porter@heliohealth.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot pricing proposal and onboarding plan

Diego,

Appreciate the plan — this looks close, but procurement pushed back hard on the 65% off. Their ask is:

- Deeper unit discount through first 4 weeks (effectively 75% off) as a ramp encouragement
- Limit our exposure with a hard monthly spend cap of $35k
- Standard MSA redlines attached from legal (see attached)

If Redwood can do option A with a 75% front-loaded discount and a $35k hard cap for month 1-3, we can sign quickly. Our procurement is procurement@heliohealth.com — they'll need final numbers for the PO.

Thanks,
Jane
Sr. Product Lead, HelioHealth

Attachments:
- HelioHealth_MSA_redlines.pdf (pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Escalation — HelioHealth wants deeper front-loaded discount + cap — need VP/CFO go/no-go

Team,

Forwarding Helio's reply — procurement now requires a front-loaded 75% discount for weeks 1–4, and a hard monthly cap of $35k for months 1–3. Legal also returned redlines (attached). This is outside our standard commercial playbook for pilots due to both the depth of discount and the explicit hard cap (risking consumption vs fixed revenue).

Quick math (conservative):
- Estimated pilot consumption at list: 10M tokens/month * $0.010 = $100,000/month list equivalent
- Under requested Option A (75% front-loaded): month 1 at $0.0025/token -> $25,000 (heavy front-loaded subsidy)

Options and impact (see attached pricing_impact tab):

Option A (aggressive):
- 12-week pilot; weeks 1–4 at 75% off list; weeks 5–12 at 65% off.
- One-time onboarding credit $15k
- Revenue impact vs list: estimated realized revenue ~$38k vs list ~$270k for the pilot period (gross delta ~-$232k)
- Pros: gets the deal over line quickly, high expansion upside
- Cons: significant short-term margin hit and precedent risk

Option B (compromise, recommended):
- 12-week pilot; weeks 1–4 at 70% off; weeks 5–12 at 60% off
- Hard monthly cap at $35k for months 1–3, with a true-up clause: if usage exceeds cap by >20% we bill the excess at list rates thereafter
- Onboarding credit $10k
- Estimated realized revenue ~$94k vs list ~$270k

Recommendation: Approve Option B with explicit true-up and a contractual cap to protect us — require CFO signoff on the cap/true-up language. If leadership opts to prioritize velocity over near-term economics, approve Option A but require a post-pilot commercial conversion milestone to be included in the MA.

Attachments: Draft_MSA_redlines.pdf; Pricing_Options_A_B.csv; HelioHealth_Pilot_MA_plan.xlsx

Request: Can I get VP/CFO conditional signoff by Tue EOD 3/22? We need to respond to procurement to keep deal momentum.

Thanks,
Diego
